title: Collect every vCenter authorization role in stable order
prompt:
Platform engineering needs a reproducible vCenter authorization-role inventory even when the server splits the collection across several pages and returns roles in an arbitrary order. Complete `VcfVcenterRoleCollection/VcfVcenterRoleCollection.psm1`.

Read the protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The focused contract was projected directly from `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the immutable VCF 9.1 commit recorded in both files. The YAML specification, not a rendered documentation page, is the wire authority. The only operationId in scope is exactly `Vcenter.Authorization.Roles_list`.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 is installed by the environment. Keep the supplied manifest prerequisite on `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` version `13.5.0.25380678`; it supplies the OpenAPI server-connection contract used by the module. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, or replace any VMware module, SDK assembly, binding, or OpenAPI file. Issue the requests with `System.Net.Http.HttpClient`; the implementation must not contain `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, `Start-Process`, `curl`, or `Connect-VIServer`.

Preserve the supplied signatures and export exactly these commands:

- `New-VcfVcenterRoleClient` accepts either an authenticated `VMware.Sdk.OpenApi.Cmdlets.IServerConnection` (with an optional `-Server` URI override) or the loopback-friendly `-Server <uri> -SessionToken <string>` form. In the connection form, reuse the HTTP client returned by the connection's `.GetClient()` method. `-SkipCertificateCheck` belongs only to the token form. Creating a client performs no API request.
- `Get-VcfVcenterRoleCollection -Client <object> [-PageSize <int64>]` retrieves the complete collection. `PageSize` defaults to the specification default of 200 and must be positive.

Send only `GET /api/vcenter/authorization/roles`. On every request put `page_size` first. Omit `marker` from the first request; if a response contains a non-empty marker, request the next page with that marker percent-encoded and placed after `page_size`. Continue until a response omits marker. Send `Accept: application/json`, authenticate with `vmware-api-session-id`, send no request body, and fail every non-2xx response.

Do not send a filter object or any `is_system`, `names`, or `privileges` query field. Every unset optional field must be absent rather than null, an empty string, an empty array, false, or an SDK default. Reject a null page, missing or null `items`, a null item, a blank `role`, missing `info`, a blank `info.name`, a non-string marker, an empty marker, a non-empty marker paired with an empty page, or a repeated marker.

Buffer all pages before returning. Return every item sorted first by `info.name` using `StringComparer.Ordinal`, then by `role` using `StringComparer.Ordinal`; do not trust server or page order.

Run `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File .protected/verify.ps1`. The protected verifier creates runtime-only tokens, markers, and role records, starts the contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, and reads its fsynced request log. It checks the exact method, path, query order and escaping, page continuity, authentication header, JSON accept header, empty body, complete results, ordinal order, and omission of every unset optional field. It never contacts a live VMware endpoint. Everything under `.protected/` and `docs/`, plus the module manifest, is protected; edit only `VcfVcenterRoleCollection/VcfVcenterRoleCollection.psm1`.
scenario: the vCenter role collection spans three marker-linked pages whose records are deliberately out of order; the client must preserve marker continuity, omit every unset filter, collect all items, and emit one ordinally sorted result
constraint: the loopback fixture derives its sole allow-listed route from the protected contract and its fsynced log proves exact query order, marker escaping, header shape, empty bodies, and optional-field omission
